### 1. What the customer states, and what the simulator may do

From `user_scenario`: Nadia R. Kowalczyk rings about one thing — *"I'm trying to find out whether there's any way of getting my ring finished sooner - our anniversary is on the third of October and I'd rather not spend it without the ring."*

- Target object: named only as "my ring" / the engagement ring left at the workshop "in the middle of June"; **she has no work order number** — *"the yellow slip is somewhere in a kitchen drawer and asks the agent to find it under her name instead."* The object must be found from the records.
- Timing: she needs it before **3 October**; she rings on 2026-09-17.
- Boundary of the action: she will not agree to anything open-ended — *"she will not agree to anything open-ended. If the agent tells her there is a figure she has to agree to before the bench can carry on, she wants to hear the figure first; once she has heard it she says yes."*
- Mode of authorisation: she performs the step herself when it is handed to her — *"when the agent hands the step over to her she carries it out herself and reads back what comes of it."* This is the `owner=user` tool pattern.
- The simulator is passive and conditional throughout: it gives the phone number when asked how to find her (`4155553317`), date of birth `1984-03-22` only if more is wanted, licence last four `3342` only if one more thing is wanted, *"one at a time and only when they are asked for"*; it mentions the care plan and the Circle card **only if the agent asks about coverage or membership**, and cannot quote a number from either. It never names a tool, a policy or a next step. It does state one checkable fact conditionally — what she put down in June — as a cross-check, not as an answer.
- She consents to desk-side action generally: *"you do whatever you need to do on your side"*, and accepts the expedited charge once told: *"if that's what it costs to have it for the third, then go ahead."*

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with inputs, intermediates and value

Master Jeweler Service level figures read from the tariff/facet documents: bench rate 185.00; rush share **30 %**; out-of-hours charge **185.00**; notice 48 h; target turnaround **10 business days**; rush turnaround 4 business days; estimate validity **45 calendar days**; stone release threshold **5,000.00**; care and custody cover cap 40,000.00; member discount 5 %; insured shipping 35.00.

**(A) The amount the protection claim answers for — `covered_amount`.**
Computation document: `measuring_what_coverage_answers_for_6ab6ea5c` — *"What the coverage answers for is the measured bench labour taken at the share the coverage carries less any step taken off that share, and it is never more than the amount standing on the priced line the credit is measured against, nor more than the benefit still available on the coverage; the figure is rounded to the nearest cent."*

| Input | Tier taken and the return that put it there | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Measured bench labour | `bench_labour_measured_net_of_amounts_taken_off_69846d05` cl. 1 — amounts already taken off (`bbf91d65-…` −96.20, `1a2a530d-…` −101.40) **and** coverage in force (`status='active'`, `expiry_date='2027-10-15'` later than 2026-09-17) → *"net of every amount already taken off the order"* | 2,757.30 − 197.60 = **2,559.70** |
| Share the coverage carries | `coverage_share_on_repeat_claims_and_lapsed_inspections_84384d60` cl. 1 — *"The coverage stands in force and a claim has already been settled against it"*: `claims_settled_count=1`, ledger row `10aa9049-…` `protection_claim_settled` `claim_outcome='settled_full'` | **70 %** |
| Step off the share | `claim_frequency_step_off_coverage_share_4b150e8c` cl. 1 — claims *standing filed* in the twelve months to 2026-09-17 (window opens 2025-09-17): `CL-318902` filed 2026-01-22 and `CL-330871` filed 2026-09-05 = **more than one**, coverage in force → frequent-claim step | **8 %** |
| Line the credit is measured against | `priced_line_a_coverage_credit_is_measured_against_a902bee4` cl. 1 — a check that found rework needed stands (`b59f10e6-…`, `quality_check_result='rework_required'`) and coverage in force → *"the largest bench labour line standing on the work order"* = `33a46ca9-…` | **1,924.00** |
| Benefit still available | protection plan `remaining_benefit_allowance` | **2,800.00** |

2,559.70 × (70 % − 8 %) = 2,559.70 × 0.62 = 1,587.014 → **1,587.01**. Lowest of 1,587.01 / 1,924.00 / 2,800.00 = **1,587.01**.
Call: `apply_claim_coverage_f28c459e{service_order_id='c73faeec-…', customer_id='b1a6fc32-…', protection_claim_reference='CL-330871', source_entry_id='33a46ca9-4b15-4d7c-90fc-31d20b6b7e3f', covered_amount=1587.01}`.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**The customer named one problem**: have the ring finished sooner. Reading the KB from there:

**Hop 1 — expedited handling waits on a confirmed ceiling (state-derived).**
`expedited_handling_charge_on_a_work_order_5d728f78` states, in the blocked policy's own rule: *"The charge for expedited handling is priced only after the work order carries an authorisation the customer has confirmed on the day the expedited handling is taken on."* That names a **record-visible state** of the work order, not an action. Checking the records: `find_service_intake{customer_id}` returns exactly one request, `a6869385-…`, `request_type='estimate_authorization'`, `request_status='customer_confirmed'`, `authorized_amount=3200.0`, `effective_date='2026-06-25'`. The only confirmed authorisation runs from 2026-06-25, not from the day the expedited handling is taken on (2026-09-17). **The state does not hold.** Searching with the words the sentence and the records use — "authorisation", "the ceiling the bench may run up to", "confirmed" — reaches `authorised_ceiling_for_work_at_the_bench_a4f80678`, whose own rule describes the write that brings that state about: *"One call puts a confirmed authorisation on the workshop desk's request record for the named work order, carrying the ceiling agreed and taking effect from today. The record is written as an authorisation the customer has confirmed rather than one merely taken down."* The ceiling to be agreed is worked out in `bench_total_answered_for_and_allowance_d7505c1e`. **Mark: state-derived.**

**Hop 2 — the ceiling waits on the claim credit standing recorded (state-derived).**
`authorised_ceiling_for_work_at_the_bench_a4f80678` states, in its own rule: *"The ceiling is fixed only after every amount a protection claim answers for on the work order stands recorded against the priced line it answers for. Until the work order shows every amount a protection claim answers for standing recorded against the priced line it answers for, the ceiling is not fixed."* Again a record-visible state. Checking the records: the work order carries `protection_claim_reference='CL-330871'`; the protection ledger shows `7bdd809f-…` `protection_claim_filed` on 2026-09-05 for `CL-330871`, `covered_item_sku='RING-52704'`, `service_order_reference='WO-441907'`, with no denial or refusal row against it (the only refusal in the ledger is `4d9bd89e-…` against the different claim `CL-318902`); and the service ledger carries **no** coverage entry at all — no row bears `protection_claim_reference='CL-330871'` or a coverage event type. **The state does not hold.** Searching with the sentence's own words — "an amount a protection claim answers for", "recorded against the priced line" — reaches `protection_claim_credit_on_work_order_2c85887e`: *"what the coverage answers for is worked out on the bench labour standing priced on that work order and is taken off the order as a single credit recorded against one priced line. The credit is recorded against the priced line it is measured against."* That is the write that brings the waited-on state about; its conditions (*"a protection claim that stands filed against the covered piece, has been sent to the workshop under that work order's reference and has not been refused"*) are all satisfied by the rows above. The figure is worked in `measuring_what_coverage_answers_for_6ab6ea5c`. **Mark: state-derived.**

**Hop 3 — nothing further.** `protection_claim_credit_on_work_order_2c85887e` states no prerequisite sentence of its own; its conditions are met on the records as they stand. The recursion terminates.

**Resulting tree and handling order.**
```
apply the protection claim credit  (root of the chain, unnamed by the customer)
        ↓ brings about: "every amount a protection claim answers for stands recorded against the priced line it answers for"
confirm the authorised ceiling     (customer's own write)
        ↓ brings about: "the work order carries an authorisation the customer has confirmed on the day"
price the expedited handling       (the only thing the customer asked about)
```
Direction of dependency: expedited → ceiling → claim credit. Handling order: claim credit, then ceiling, then expedited charge. Both hops **state-derived**; **no hop was pre-solved** — no document names another problem's tool, no document states the chain, and neither prerequisite sentence names the action or the performer that resolves it.

### Two-way counter-proof

**(i) The visible materials fully support the conclusion.** Every figure above comes from a quoted document sentence plus a quoted record field; no step required a fact that was not returned by a finder call or printed in a published document.

**(ii) The closest alternative on each boundary is excluded by a visible sentence or record.**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Work the surcharge on `authorized_total=3200.0` (the "authorised bench total") | `expedited_handling_notice_and_same_day_work_250b1662` records as **no longer in force** *"that expedited handling shortens the promised date to the level's rush turnaround and carries the level's surcharge on the authorised bench total"*; the in-force basis, `expedited_handling_charge_on_a_work_order_5d728f78`, works it *"on the ceiling standing on the most recent authorisation the customer has confirmed"*. **But see the finding recorded in `gt_comparison`: the tariff facet still describes the rush share as a percentage of the authorised bench total.** |
| Use the June authorisation (3,200.00) as "the most recent confirmed authorisation" | It would be the most recent *only if* no new one is taken; but the same hub requires the confirmed authorisation to stand *"on the day the expedited handling is taken on"*, and `effective_date='2026-06-25'` is not that day |
| Count the time at the bench from `intake_date='2026-06-18'` for the allowance uplift | `counting_the_time_a_piece_has_been_at_the_bench_bf459799` cl. 1 moves the anchor to the most recent rework-required check where amounts have been taken off — both hold |
| Measure the coverage against the most recent labour line (101.40) | `priced_line_a_coverage_credit_is_measured_against_a902bee4` cl. 1 selects *"the largest bench labour line standing on the work order"* because a rework-required check stands and the coverage is in force |
| Take the labour as booked (2,757.30) for the coverage measure | `bench_labour_measured_net_of_amounts_taken_off_69846d05` cl. 1 measures it *"net of every amount already taken off the order"* |
| Include the −800.00 payment among the amounts taken off | `goodwill_amounts_and_member_labour_discount_237cc6ef` enumerates amounts taken off as goodwill / member benefit / guarantee; `payment_shipping_and_appraisal_updates_fa15c13e` treats a payment as reducing the balance, not as an amount taken off |
| Take the member relief off the expedited charge alone | `where_member_relief_is_taken_off_expedited_charges_9894e5e1` row 1 applies, a `circle_benefit_redeemed` row standing within the window |
| Price the surcharge without the out-of-hours charge | `charge_for_holding_the_bench_open_out_of_hours_f75c41ea` row *(yes, yes)* charges the level's own figure in full on these two records |
| Refuse for want of notice, or refuse the piece | Notice 48 h at this level against sixteen days; declared value 18,500.00 inside the 40,000.00 ceiling; release already signed |
| Include the delivered Priority Bench order | `several_orders_for_one_customer_a2fea659`: *"each is priced, authorised and delivered on its own and no balance is moved between them"* |

**(iii) The natural wrong answer — "she asked only to have it hurried, so only hurry it" — is excluded.** Doing only the expedited charge means calling `charge_expedite_surcharge_af83d9eb` while the work order carries no authorisation the customer has confirmed on this day; `expedited_handling_charge_on_a_work_order_5d728f78` says in terms that the charge *"is priced only after"* that state stands, so the visible principle does not allow the resulting state. Pushing back one hop, confirming a ceiling now without first recording what `CL-330871` answers for leaves the ceiling in a state `authorised_ceiling_for_work_at_the_bench_a4f80678` calls *"not fixed"*, and the figure would be wrong by the whole credit. The exclusion comes from prerequisite sentences standing on the blocked side, which is the source's own form — not from any route, tool name or chain.

### KB-RUNTIME RED — the uplifted allowance is not pinned to the cent by any visible document

**Symptom.** From the published documents alone the ceiling comes to **1,422.56** and the expedited surcharge to **448.16**; the source's scored values are **1,422.57** and **448.17**. Two of this task's three scored parameters are wrong by one cent for a reader who has the whole corpus and every record.

**Root cause.** The rounding moment that produces the gold cent exists only in the hidden compute binding. The source's `service_ext_revised_authorization.compute` carries

```
uplifted_allowance: RND(allowance * K('delayed_uplift'), 2)   # = round(359.90 * 1.25, 2) = 449.88
result:             RND(net_bench_total + uplifted_allowance, 2)   # = 972.69 + 449.88 = 1422.57
```

i.e. the **uplifted** allowance is itself rounded to the cent before it is added to the bench total. No published document states that. `bench_total_answered_for_and_allowance_d7505c1e` names exactly two rounding moments — *"That bench total taken at the allowance rate and rounded to the nearest cent"* and *"the bench total … plus the allowance, rounded to the nearest cent"* — and `allowance_uplift_for_long_bench_time_and_repeat_checks_a39bde57` states the multiple with no rounding at all: *"the allowance is taken a quarter as much again — at a multiple of 1.25"*. Its one worked figure, *"an allowance of 80.00 USD taken a quarter as much again comes to 100.00 USD"*, is a clean number and reveals nothing.

**Evidence — the two readings the visible corpus admits, on this task's world.**
- Bench total answered for = 2,757.30 − 197.60 − 1,587.01 = **972.69**; allowance rate 20 + 5 + 3 + 9 = **37 %**; allowance = 972.69 × 37 % = 359.8953 → **359.90** (the one rounding the baseline document names).
- *Reading A, the literal sequence of the documents*: the uplift is applied to that allowance and nothing rounds the product — 359.90 × 1.25 = **449.875** — so the ceiling is 972.69 + 449.875 = **1,422.565**, and the single rounding the document names is the one on the ceiling. Rounded half to even at the cent — the mode the corpus itself names, in the `authorized_ceiling` row of `authorised_ceiling_for_work_at_the_bench_a4f80678`: *"USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the cent"* — 1,422.565 gives **1,422.56**.
- *Reading B*: the uplifted figure is still "the allowance", so the baseline's *"rounded to the nearest cent"* attaches to it — 449.875 → **449.88** — and the ceiling is **1,422.57**, the gold.
- The corpus does not decide between them, and the reading that follows the documents' own order of sentences, with the documents' own rounding mode, is the one that is wrong.
- The error then propagates through the expedited charge unchanged: on 1,422.56 the charge is 312.96 + 185.00 = 497.96, less 10 % = 448.16, under a cap of 569.02; on 1,422.57 it is 312.97 + 185.00 = 497.97, less 10 % = **448.17**, under a cap of 569.03.

**Affected documents and locations.**
- `env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/docs/service/allowance_uplift_for_long_bench_time_and_repeat_checks_a39bde57.json`, section "## The uplift" and the closing line of "## Worked on hypothetical inputs" — the method tier states the multiplier but not the rounding mode, precision or moment the source's binding pins.
- `env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/docs/service/bench_total_answered_for_and_allowance_d7505c1e.json`, "## The quantities" → *"The allowance for the work still to come"*, and "## The ceiling" — the two rounding moments named there do not cover the product of the uplift.
- Consequently `env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/docs/service/expedited_charge_on_the_confirmed_ceiling_accb4af3.json` yields 448.16 rather than 448.17, though that document is itself faithful.

**Nature, stated honestly.** The omission is inherited rather than invented by the rendering: the source's own `rule` and `baseline.rule` prose for `service_ext_revised_authorization` is equally silent — it says *"The allowance for the work still to come is that bench total taken at the allowance rate and rounded to the nearest cent … The allowance is taken as it stands … The ceiling is the bench total … plus the allowance, rounded to the nearest cent"* — and only the `compute` binding rounds the uplifted figure. So the scored cent is reachable only from hidden compute, which is exactly the condition this part records as **KB-RUNTIME RED**. This is recorded as a policy-side note as well under `policy_kb/workshop_service_desk/0.md`, and no fix is proposed here.

**Not attributed to the solving agent.** This is not an arithmetic slip: both readings are arithmetically correct, and the corpus does not choose between them.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME RED** for task 0. The problem tree, the object, the branch, the tool sequence, the owners, the terminal state and one of the three scored parameters are entailed exactly by the visible materials; the ceiling and the expedited surcharge are not pinned to the cent by any published document.

### B-1 — the replay, under both conventions

Replayed from the published prose alone, on this task's world, using the same record values quoted in `blind_answer`:

- Bench total the customer is answering for — now *"Every bench labour line standing priced on the work order, less every amount already taken off it, less everything a protection claim has answered for on it"* — 2,757.30 − 197.60 − 1,587.01 = **972.69** (unchanged: this order carries no priced line that is not a bench labour line).
- Allowance rate 20 + 5 + 3 + 9 = 37 %; allowance = *"that bench total taken at the allowance rate and rounded to the nearest cent"* = 359.8953 → **359.90**.
- Uplift — *"the allowance is taken a quarter as much again — at a multiple of 1.25"* — 359.90 × 1.25 = 449.875; then the new sentence, *"Whatever multiple the allowance is taken at, the figure it comes to is rounded to the nearest cent before it is added to the bench total"* → **449.88 under half-to-even and 449.88 under half-up; the two conventions agree**.
- Ceiling = *"the bench total … plus the allowance, rounded to the nearest cent"* = 972.69 + 449.88 = **1,422.57**, no tie to break.
- Surcharge = 1,422.57 × 22 % = **312.97**, plus the out-of-hours charge 185.00 = 497.97, less 10 % relief taken off the two together = 448.173 → **448.17**, under a cap of 1,422.57 × 40 % = 569.03.

| | half-to-even | half-up |

| **round-2 corpus** ceiling / surcharge | **1,422.57 / 448.17** | **1,422.57 / 448.17** |

The pair demonstrated in revision 1 has collapsed to a single value, and that value is the source's. The mechanism is exactly the one the finding named: moving the rounding to its own moment means the tie that has to be broken is 449.875 — where both conventions give 449.88 — instead of 1,422.565, where they disagreed. A reader of the visible corpus alone now reaches one answer on this world whichever convention they carry.

**Residual, recorded rather than passed over.** The prose still says "rounded to the nearest cent" without naming the tie-break; the convention is named only in the tool parameter row (*"rounded half to even at the cent"*), as it was in round 1 and as it is throughout this corpus and throughout the source, whose `RND` is the same everywhere. On this task's world the two conventions agree at every rounding the computation performs, so uniqueness holds and this is not a defect here. It is noted so that a future world where they diverge is not assumed to be covered.
